key_insight: Pooled multi-cohort transfer learning improved intracranial 4D Flow MRI super-resolution accuracy over cohort-specific training and synthetic pretraining alone.
clinical_relevance: Improved vessel depiction and velocity reconstruction agreement could support cerebrovascular imaging research, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Pretrained a convolutional neural network on synthetic cerebrovascular data.
Fine-tuned with cohort-specific or pooled in vivo MRI data.
Evaluated voxel-wise reconstruction using high-resolution-derived inputs and angiographic performance using native standard-resolution scans.
evidence_signal: Among 18 participants with paired 1.2-mm and 0.6-mm scans, pooled training achieved mean velocity-normalized RMSE of 0.119 versus 0.127 for cohort-specific models and 0.147 for synthetic pretraining.
watch_item: The small sample—including only three participants each with moyamoya disease and multiple sclerosis—requires larger, multi-center validation.
paper_title: Toward Clinical Translation of Deep Learning-Based Intracranial Super-Resolution 4D Flow MRI Using Multi-Cohort Transfer Learning
